pulverize

/PUL-ver-ize/ — stress on first syllable, rhymes with 'size' · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To pulverize something is to smash or crush it so completely that it breaks into tiny fragments or powder.

The machine pulverizes old concrete into gravel for new roads.

Example

The industrial blender pulverizes fresh coffee beans into fine powder in seconds, filling the air with rich aroma.

Pulverize is more precise than 'crush' or 'grind' because it specifically means breaking something into tiny fragments or powder—emphasizing both the completeness and extreme fineness of the destruction. 'Crush' might just mean compressing; grinding is more mechanical and controlled.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

crush: To crush is to press hard until something breaks apart — one strong squeeze, like a can under a boot. To pulverize goes much further down the scale of size: not just broken, but reduced to tiny fragments or powder, with nothing solid left.

grind: To grind is to wear something down into small particles between two surfaces — steady, controlled, and stoppable at any coarseness. To pulverize is the extreme finish: smashing or crushing something so completely that only fine powder remains.

fragment: To fragment is to break into scattered small pieces — a dropped plate fragments into shards you could still glue back together. To pulverize destroys even the pieces: what is left is powder or dust, far too fine to ever reassemble.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

consolidate: combine into a single solid whole

assemble: put separate parts together into one

Where it sits · how fine the pieces become

crack → crumble → shatter → pulverize

crack vs. pulverize: Crack is far weaker than pulverize; crack only splits a surface, while pulverize smashes something all the way into tiny fragments or powder.

crumble vs. pulverize: Crumble is milder than pulverize; crumble breaks something into small pieces gently, while pulverize crushes it right down to dust.

shatter vs. pulverize: Shatter is strong, but pulverize is stronger still; shatter breaks something into sharp shards, while pulverize grinds it into fine powder.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — pulver-: dust, powder (Latin)

Suffix — -ize: to make, to turn into (Greek/Latin)

Put it together: Pulver- means 'dust or powder' and -ize means 'to turn into,' so to pulverize is to smash something so completely that it turns to powder.

Use the root in a new word: powder: The climbers dipped their hands in chalk powder before starting up the wall.

Word Choice

neutral / technical

Pulverize is the word when something is broken down into tiny pieces or powder—usually in an industrial or mechanical context. For gentler breaking or less extreme results, use 'crush' or 'grind' instead.
